basis: Embryopathy in non-PKU offspring: microcephaly/intellectual disability and congenital heart defects define it; maternal metabolic disease is not the child's diagnosis.
Intellectual disability and microcephaly define CNS involvement; optic atrophy defines ocular involvement. Short stature alone does not establish skeletal disease.
Cortisol-secreting adrenal cortical adenoma; Cushing syndrome and hypertension are separately diagnosed conditions, not additional direct organ involvement.
Congenital cranial nerve synkinesis causes jaw-triggered eyelid ptosis; both eyelid dysfunction and abnormal oculomotor innervation define the disorder.
Facial nerve/movement disorder causing rippling contractions; contractions alone do not establish direct skeletal muscle damage.
Aggressive periodontitis destroys gingival and tooth-supporting tissues through bacterial biofilm-driven immune inflammation; oral tissues are gastrointestinal.
Metabolic beta-oxidation defects; neurologic injury typical across subtypes (inferred >30%); hepatic disease varies. [Orphanet](https://www.orpha.net/ORDO/Orphanet_79188)
Zygomaticomaxillary cleft and lower-eyelid coloboma are defining structural lesions. [Orphanet](https://www.orpha.net/ORDO/Orphanet_141265)
Progressive distal myopathy defines the disease; persistent distal sensory impairment occurs in 80-99%, supporting additional neurologic functional loss.
Toxin-induced damage to multiple peripheral nerves; other toxic organ injuries depend on the exposure and are not inherent to this concept.
Disease of the tympanic membrane, part of the ear; infection is not shared by all subtypes.
Syndactyly and intellectual disability define the syndrome. Hirsutism, thick hair and dermatoglyphic differences do not establish damaging skin disease.
Congenital failure of normal femoral bone continuity with a false joint; a skeletal disorder.
Definition specifies autoimmune inflammation and fibrosis of bile ducts; associated ulcerative colitis is a separate disease.
Corticospinal degeneration defines SPG6; pes cavus, muscle atrophy and fixed joint limitation are frequent (30-79%). Bladder symptoms alone do not establish urinary damage.
Type 1 explicitly denotes isolated uterovaginal aplasia, outside the axes. Renal annotations conflict with this definition and should not override the isolated subtype.
Exfoliative skin disease; malabsorption 80-99%; respiratory insufficiency alone does not establish direct lung damage. [Orphanet](https://www.orpha.net/en/disease/sign/1954)
DZIP1L-related renal cystic dysplasia; hypertension (5/7) is a secondary, separately diagnosed disease; hepatosplenomegaly occurs in only 1/7.
Chronic noninfectious anterior uveitis with iris atrophy and inflammatory cells; immune-mediated ocular inflammation defines the disease.
Hypomyelinating leukodystrophy and chondrodysplasia define the disease; cleft palate occurs in 1/2 reported patients. Nystagmus alone does not establish direct ocular damage.
Neoplasm arising in or occupying the ear; no additional organ involvement is common across this broad group.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome with intellectual/developmental and speech impairment; other organ anomalies vary. [NIH](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gtr/conditions/C6065891/)
Mammary origin inferred from conventional comedocarcinoma classification; breast has no axis. [NCI](https://tp53.cancer.gov/morph)
Chorea is a neurologic movement disorder; involuntary muscle contractions do not imply primary muscle disease or damage to other organs.
Intellectual disability, epilepsy and postaxial polydactyly define the syndrome; oral, skin and ear anomalies are occasional or nondamaging.
